title: SAML assertion binding and attribute verification in audit events
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Problem: Current audit events capture admin actions and coarse SSO linkages but do not reliably record the SAML assertion context needed to reconstruct authorization decisions or to debug mismatched attribute-based roles. This ticket defines an audit event shape and logging taxonomy to: 1) bind SAML assertions to audit events without logging full PII-bearing XML blobs in the main event stream, 2) record per-attribute verification outcomes (what was asserted, what was checked, and whether the attribute was trusted), and 3) provide a compact, replayable reference to full assertion material stored under encryption when required for incident/post-mortem.

Goals:
- Produce a minimal, safe audit envelope that allows engineers and auditors to correlate an admin action with the exact identity assertions used for that decision.
- Preserve privacy and compliance by avoiding storage of unredacted assertion payloads in high-throughput event indexes.
- Make attribute verification explicit so RBAC v2 policy evaluation can be debugged deterministically.

Proposed event fields (human-readable description; implement as top-level event properties):
- event_id: opaque UUID for the audit record.
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC.
- event_type: e.g., admin.role.change, policy.update, session.grant.
- tenant_id / org_id: multitenancy context.
- actor_id: internal user id (if available).
- actor_type: human | service | external_identity_provider.
- actor_display_name: display string.
- saml_assertion_fingerprint: sha256 hex of the canonicalized SAML assertion. (Used to bind but not reveal XML).
- saml_issuer: issuer entityID from the assertion.
- saml_subject_nameid: normalized NameID value or 'absent'.
- saml_audience: asserted audience(s) as comma-separated string (if present).
- saml_attributes_summary: short serialized list of attribute keys present (e.g. "groups:3, email:present, role:present").
- saml_attribute_verification: compact encoded list describing per-attribute result, using triples encoded as key|method|result where result in {verified,unverified,mismatched,absent}. Example: "email|idp-claims|verified,groups|idp-claims|verified,department|claim-check|mismatched".
- assertion_storage_ref: optional opaque reference id to an encrypted blob in the assertion vault when full assertion needs retention for >30d. The event contains the ref, not the raw XML.
- session_id and request_id: trace linkage for request flow.
- action_target: short string describing the resource (e.g., policy:12345).
- change_diff: compact normalized JSON Patch string or base64-encoded compressed patch when >1024 bytes.
- intent_token: if the action was mediated by a UI or API workflow that supplied an intent, include its id.
- outcome: success | failure | partial, plus short reason.
- retention_class: e.g., default | pii-sensitive | long-term-audit.
- redaction_hints: comma-separated list of fields to mask when exporting (e.g., "saml_subject_nameid,email").

Taxonomy: what to log and when:
- Authentication events: record assertion_fingerprint, issuer, attribute_summary, verification results on every successful SAML login and every login that leads to an elevated admin session.
- Authorization decisions that use attributes: record the exact attribute verification snapshot at the time of the decision (saml_attribute_verification) and the policy version id used.
- Admin resource mutations: record change_diff plus assertion fingerprint and assertion_storage_ref if the change modifies identity configuration, roles, or policies.
- Delegation or impersonation actions: include delegator_id, delegatee_id, and the originating assertion fingerprint for accountability.

Privacy & storage rules:
- Never store raw SAML XML in the high-index event stream. Only store sha256(assertion) and a short attribute summary.
- When full assertion is needed (regulatory/legal/incident), write the raw assertion to an encrypted assertion vault (separate AES-GCM encrypted store with HSM-wrapped keys) and keep only an assertion_storage_ref in the event. Access to the vault requires explicit audit and an approval workflow.
- Redaction: any exported event for non-security teams should have redaction applied using redaction_hints.

Diff/Change format guidance:
- Use JSON Patch (RFC 6902) normalized canonical form with deterministic key ordering.
- For large diffs (>1KB), compress and store as base64 gzip, set change_diff_type to compressed+base64, and include uncompressed length.
- For simple role changes, prefer a compact change token of the form "role:+admin,-viewer" to reduce index size.

Backward compatibility and schema evolution:
- Introduce fields as optional; consumers must gracefully ignore unknown fields.
- Provide a migration job that backfills saml_assertion_fingerprint for active sessions where raw assertion logs exist in legacy stores.

Operational needs:
- Add a dedicated assertion vault service and RBAC controls for who can resolve assertion_storage_ref.
- Instrument alerts for repeated 'mismatched' attribute_verification results to catch IdP drift.
- Add coverage in the audit replay tool to accept event sets with assertion_fingerprint + assertion_storage_ref and re-run policy evaluation deterministically.

Why this is different from prior work:
- Existing tickets standardize delta formats and actor-target shapes; this ticket ties SSO/SAML fidelity to audit records with an explicit immutable assertion fingerprint and a secure storage reference pattern. It balances reproducibility and privacy by separating binding vs raw storage and by making attribute verification explicit in a compact, searchable form.
acceptance_criteria: All admin-authenticated audit events include saml_assertion_fingerprint and saml_attribute_verification or an explicit flag 'assertion_not_checked'
Attribute verification uses the key|method|result compact encoding and documented enum values
change_diff uses normalized JSON Patch or compressed base64 when >1024 bytes
Assertion vault implemented with encrypted blobs and access control; events contain assertion_storage_ref when blobs are written
E2E replay test that rehydrates assertion via assertion_storage_ref and reproduces the authorization decision in the audit replay harness
decisions: Use sha256 hex fingerprint of canonicalized SAML assertion instead of storing XML in the event stream
Store full assertions only in a separate encrypted vault, referenced by assertion_storage_ref
Encode per-attribute verification as key|method|result triples in a single string field for searchability
Use JSON Patch canonicalized form for change diffs; allow compressed base64 for large payloads
design_notes: Canonicalization rules: remove whitespace between tags, normalize attribute ordering, and canonicalize NameID formats before hashing. Hash: lowercase hex sha256 of UTF-8 bytes of canonicalized XML. Attribute verification methods: idp-claims (directly asserted by IdP), claim-check (we compared claim to authoritative source), regex-allowlist, external-lookup. Verification enum: verified, unverified, mismatched, absent. Example compact attribute_verification entry: 'email|idp-claims|verified,groups|idp-claims|verified,department|claim-check|mismatched'. Example event snippet (single-line JSON for illustration only): '{"event_id":"uuid-123","timestamp":"2026-02-15T14:05:22Z","event_type":"admin.role.change","actor_id":"u-42","saml_assertion_fingerprint":"b6f...","saml_attribute_verification":"email|idp-claims|verified,groups|idp-claims|verified","change_diff":"[{\"op\":\"add\",\"path\":\"/roles/0\",\"value\":\"admin\"}]"}'
